title: Opposite-root pairing and three-exponential reflection map
statement:
Let $A$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $r\geq0$. An $A$-group scheme means a scheme over $X$ with multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying associativity, unit and inverse diagrams, as in [def-sc-group-scheme] with this base in place of a field. Put $T=\mathbf G_{m,A}^r=\operatorname{Spec}A[M]$, $M=\mathbf Z^r$, where $A[M]=A[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_r^{\pm1}]$, $e^m=\prod_jz_j^{m_j}$, and the group law is multiplication of units. Write $\chi_m:T\to\mathbf G_{m,A}$ for the character $e^m$. Let $G$ be a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] affine finite-type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] $A$-group scheme with a closed inclusion $T\hookrightarrow G$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Assume every geometric fibre of $G$ is reductive, meaning connected [def-weil-connected-scheme] with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent closed subgroup. Unipotent means that all geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful representation. Assume $T$ is a maximal torus in every geometric fibre, where a torus over an algebraically closed field is a product of multiplicative groups and maximality is for subgroup inclusion. Put $\mathfrak g=\ker(G(A[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))\to G(A))$, with addition induced by multiplication in $G$ and scalar multiplication induced by $\epsilon\mapsto a\epsilon$. The conjugation coaction of $T$ on this tangent module is denoted $\rho$, and $\mathfrak g_m=\{v:\rho(v)=v\otimes e^m\}$. Suppose $\alpha\ne0$ and both $\mathfrak g_\alpha$ and $\mathfrak g_{-\alpha}$ are locally free of rank one, with canonical maps $\exp_{\pm\alpha}:V_{\pm\alpha}\to G$ of [lem-sfb-relative-canonical-root-exponential], where $V_{\pm\alpha}(B)=B\otimes_A\mathfrak g_{\pm\alpha}$. There are a perfect $A$-bilinear pairing $\beta_\alpha:\mathfrak g_\alpha\otimes_A\mathfrak g_{-\alpha}\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ and an $A$-group homomorphism $\alpha^\vee:\mathbf G_{m,A}\to T$ such that $\chi_\alpha(\alpha^\vee(c))=c^2$. Here perfect means that each root module identifies with the $A$-dual of the other. For every commutative $A$-algebra $B$ and generator $x$ of the free rank-one $B$-module $B\otimes_A\mathfrak g_\alpha$, let $x^{-1}\in B\otimes_A\mathfrak g_{-\alpha}$ be determined by $\beta_\alpha(x,x^{-1})=1$. Then
$$n_\alpha(x)=\exp_\alpha(x)\exp_{-\alpha}(-x^{-1})\exp_\alpha(x)\in G(B)$$
normalizes $T_B$ and satisfies
$$n_\alpha(x)t n_\alpha(x)^{-1}=t\,\alpha^\vee(\chi_\alpha(t))^{-1}$$
for every $B$-algebra $C$ and $t\in T(C)$. On every geometric fibre $\alpha^\vee$ is the usual coroot for $\alpha$ in [lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections], and $n_\alpha(x)$ represents its root reflection. The pairing, coroot and formula commute with arbitrary base change and successive base changes. Neither freeness of all the other root modules nor a globally constant root system is assumed.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Lemma 4.1.3 (rank-one centralizer), Theorem 4.2.6, pp.120-121 (perfect opposite-root pairing and coroot), and Corollary 5.1.9(1), printed pp.140-141 (three-exponential normalizer element and reflection formula). Read online; WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf.

proof.text: Write $\alpha=n a_0$ with $n>0$ and $a_0$ primitive in $M=\mathbf Z^r$. Integer elementary row operations extend $a_0$ to a basis. Thus $T_\alpha:=\ker\chi_{a_0}$ is a split codimension-one torus, closed in $T$ by the quotient Hopf algebra of def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group. On a geometric fibre $\ker\chi_\alpha=\mu_n\times\mathbf G_m^{r-1}$ in these coordinates; a map from a torus to $\mu_n$ is trivial since its character exponents have no integer torsion. Hence this is the largest subtorus killed by $\alpha$, even when the residue characteristic divides $n$. The two weights remain roots on every geometric fibre by lem-sfb-relative-tangent-weight-base-change and their rank-one hypothesis. The coordinate algebra of $G$ is finitely presented over $A$ by lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation. Apply lem-sfb-relative-torus-centralizer-normalizer to $T_\alpha\subset G$: its centralizer $H$ is smooth affine of finite presentation, closed in $G$, and commutes with arbitrary base change. On every geometric fibre, lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections identifies $H$ with the reductive rank-one centralizer for $\alpha$. Consequently $H$ has reductive fibres of semisimple rank one and $T$ remains a maximal torus in it.

proof.text:
The $T$-equivariance in lem-sfb-relative-canonical-root-exponential shows that $T_\alpha$ centralizes both exponential maps on every test algebra: $\chi_{\pm\alpha}|_{T_\alpha}=1$. Thus they factor through $H$. Apply lem-sfb-relative-rank-one-local-matrix-model to $H,T,\alpha$. On each resulting affine open write
$$u_+(a)=I+aE_{12},\quad u_-(b)=I+bE_{21},\quad h(c)=\operatorname{diag}(c,c^{-1}),$$
where $I$ is the identity matrix and $E_{ij}$ has its only nonzero entry $1$ in row $i$, column $j$; use their images in $\operatorname{PGL}_2$ when appropriate, and identity on the extra central torus. Their tangent vectors $e_+,e_-$ are bases of the two root lines. Their $T$-equivariance and tangent inclusions identify $u_\pm$ with $\exp_{\pm\alpha}$ by the uniqueness clause of the exponential node, applied to $H$ and then to $G$. Set $\beta(ae_+,be_-)=ab$ and set the local coroot equal to $h$. These are a perfect pairing and a group homomorphism, and $\chi_\alpha(h(c))=c^2$.

proof.text:
In any of these matrix models put $d=1+ab$. If $d$ is a unit, multiplication gives
$$u_+(a)u_-(b)=u_-(b/d)h(d)u_+(a/d):$$
both sides have row entries $(1+ab,a,b,1)$. The multiplication $U_-\times T\times U_+\to H$ is a monomorphism: a matrix $u_-(y)\operatorname{diag}(d_1,d_2)u_+(z)$ has entries $(d_1,d_1z,yd_1,yd_1z+d_2)$, so its entries recover $y,z,d_1,d_2$ uniquely. In $\operatorname{PGL}_2$ they recover $y,z$ and the diagonal class, since scaling all entries does not change the two ratios; equality in the sheaf quotient is equality modulo a unit scalar after an fppf covering, and the recovered coordinates then agree by lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent. The extra central torus coordinate is separately recovered. Thus these assertions hold over arbitrary rings. Intrinsically the displayed Gauss formula has lower parameter $Y/(1+\beta(X,Y))$, torus parameter $h(1+\beta(X,Y))$ and upper parameter $X/(1+\beta(X,Y))$.

proof.text: Check agreement on overlaps, refining to affine opens with bases $e,f$ of the two root lines. Let two model choices give pairings with coefficients $p=\beta(e,f)$ and $q=\beta'(e,f)$, both units. Evaluate the two Gauss identities at $X=\epsilon e$, $Y=f$ over $R[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$. Uniqueness of the lower coordinate in step 3 yields $(1-p\epsilon)f=(1-q\epsilon)f$, hence $p=q$. This equality is over the whole overlap ring, including its nilpotents. With $f$ now chosen dual to $e$, evaluate at $X=(c-1)e$, $Y=f$ for an arbitrary unit $c$ in any overlap algebra. The common Gauss denominator is $c$, so uniqueness of the torus coordinate gives $h(c)=h'(c)$. Consequently both pairings and coroots agree as morphisms on overlaps, rather than merely on geometric fibres.

proof.text: Apply lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent to the open cover of the domain $V_\alpha\times_X V_{-\alpha}$ and the target $\mathbf A^1_X$, regarded as sections of the target pulled back to that domain. It glues the local pairings. Apply it on the domain $\mathbf G_{m,X}$ with target $T$ to glue the coroots. Choose a finite principal-open refinement of the affine base cover. Its pullbacks to each domain form fpqc coverings (a finite family of flat quasi-compact open immersions covering the domain). The glued morphisms are over $X$ because their composites to $X$ agree on this cover and hence globally by the same uniqueness clause. The same uniqueness clause detects all defining identities on these covers: bilinearity, the group-homomorphism identities, and $\chi_\alpha\circ\alpha^\vee(c)=c^2$. The inverses of the two duality maps glue too, since inverses are unique, so the global pairing is perfect. On the affine base its global-sections pairing is the required $A$-bilinear isomorphism $\mathfrak g_\alpha\otimes_A\mathfrak g_{-\alpha}\to A$.

proof.text:
For a generator $x$ after $A\to B$, on any pulled-back matrix chart write $x=a e_+$ with $a\in B^\times$. Then $x^{-1}=a^{-1}e_-$ and direct multiplication gives
$$u_+(a)u_-(-a^{-1})u_+(a)=w(a):=\begin{pmatrix}0&a\\-a^{-1}&0\end{pmatrix}.$$
For $t=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,d_2)$ one has
$$w(a)t w(a)^{-1}=\operatorname{diag}(d_2,d_1)=t\,h(d_1/d_2)^{-1}.$$
In $\operatorname{SL}_2$ impose $d_2=d_1^{-1}$; in $\operatorname{PGL}_2$ use the diagonal class with representative $\operatorname{diag}(c,1)$, giving $h(c)=[\operatorname{diag}(c,c^{-1})]$. The central factor is fixed. Thus this is exactly $t\alpha^\vee(\chi_\alpha(t))^{-1}$ in all models, over every further algebra $C$. This map of $T$ is involutive: its $\alpha$-character is $\chi_\alpha(t)^{-1}$ since $\chi_\alpha\circ\alpha^\vee(c)=c^2$. Conjugation therefore preserves $T$ as a subgroup scheme, in both directions. The sheaf uniqueness of lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent identifies these local equalities over $C$, proving the global normalizer assertion and displayed formula.

proof.text: On a geometric fibre the coroot and the nonidentity normalizer class just computed are the usual ones: apply the unique-reflection and unique-coroot clauses of lem-sfb-reductive-rank-one-reflections to $G,T$ and its centralizer $H$. In the matrix models $w(a)$ swaps the two root characters, so it is the nonidentity class even in characteristic two. The tangent-weight comparisons in lem-sfb-relative-tangent-weight-base-change and exponential maps in lem-sfb-relative-canonical-root-exponential commute with every algebra extension. Pull back the chosen local matrix charts along any $A\to B$: their pairings and coroots are still the constructions in step 2. The overlap uniqueness calculation of step 4 works over every ring $B$, without Noetherianity. It therefore identifies the pullback constructions with those constructed over $B$ and with any further pullback over $C$. The inverse dual vector and the three-factor product are preserved as well, by their formulas and uniqueness. This proves arbitrary and successive base-change compatibility, without trivializing any other root module or fixing its weights globally.
